title: Circular Component Dependencies (ADP Violation)
pattern: Two compiled units, crates, or modules contain dependency arrows pointing at each other, creating a cyclic dependency graph at the component level.
why_bad: It violates the Acyclic Dependencies Principle (ADP). It merges the two modules into a single large component. They can no longer be released, compiled, or tested independently.
detection: Module import analyzer identifying a cycle (`A` imports `B` which imports `A`) at compile time.
counterexample: Mutually recursive functions that are tightly localized within the exact same file and private scope.
source: Robert C. Martin, *Clean Architecture* (2017), Chapter 14 ("ADP: The Acyclic Dependencies Principle").
